result: Loss of DLK and/or LZK, singly or in combination, does not affect postnatal development of Purkinje cells. LZK KO mice generated by CRISPR deletion of the kinase domain are viable and show normal cerebellar architecture, Purkinje cell number, morphology, and molecular layer thickness at P60. Similarly, conditional deletion of DLK and/or LZK in Purkinje cells using PvalbCre shows no discernible defects in cerebellar development, Purkinje cell number, molecular layer thickness, astrocyte reactivity, or body weight.
evaluation: Claims C5, C29, C35-C47 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including histological analysis (Figure 1A), Calbindin immunostaining (Figure 1A-C), molecular layer thickness measurements (Figure 1D), GFAP staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I-J), and body weight measurements (Figure 1—figure supplement 1K). The data consistently show no phenotypic differences between knockout/conditional deletion mice and controls across multiple genotypes and timepoints.

result: Activating DLK in Purkinje cells causes rapid, early-onset degeneration through JNK activation and apoptosis. Transgenic mice (Hipp11-DLK(iOE)) were generated with Cre-inducible DLK expression. PvalbCre/+;Hipp11-DLK(iOE)/+ mice show gross abnormalities by P6, smaller body size, abnormal movements, death by P21, smaller cerebella, abnormal lobular morphology, ~98% Purkinje cell loss by P21, significantly thinner molecular layer from P10-P21, and increased astrocyte and microglia reactivity.
evaluation: Claims C6, C30, C49-C64, C70 are strongly supported by comprehensive data including body weight measurements (Figure 2A-B), cerebellar area quantification (Figure 2C), Calbindin immunostaining showing Purkinje cell loss (Figure 2D-E), molecular layer thickness measurements (Figure 2F), histological analysis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B), and GFAP/IBA1 staining showing gliosis (Figure 2—figure supplement 2C-F). The temporal progression and severity of degeneration are well-documented.

result: DLK overexpression activates JNK signaling and induces apoptosis in Purkinje cells. Elevated DLK expression substantially increases p-c-Jun in Purkinje cells at P6. TUNEL assays show apoptotic cells peak around P15 in PvalbCre/+;Hipp11-DLK(iOE)/+ mice, with some TUNEL signals co-localizing with tdTomato-labeled Purkinje cells. A significant portion of Purkinje cells at P15 are positive for cleaved caspase-3.
evaluation: Claims C65-C69 are supported by p-c-Jun immunostaining (Figure 3A-B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1), TUNEL assays showing temporal progression of apoptosis (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C), and cleaved caspase-3 staining (Figure 3C-D). The data demonstrate both JNK pathway activation and apoptotic cell death markers in Purkinje cells.

result: DLK overexpression disrupts the dendritic cytoskeleton in Purkinje cells. DLK is expressed in somas, dendrites, and axons of Purkinje cells. A substantial portion of Purkinje cells show dendrite swelling, with ~65% of cells with swelling positive for cleaved caspase-3. Dendrite swelling peaks around P15. MAP2 levels are significantly decreased in dendrites, and NF-200 levels are decreased in axons and dendrites.
evaluation: Claims C73-C76, C78-C80 are supported by DLK immunostaining (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), Calbindin staining showing dendrite swelling (Figure 3C,E), quantification of swelling and caspase-3 co-localization (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 4), MAP2 immunostaining (Figure 3G), and NF-200 immunostaining (Figure 3H). The data consistently demonstrate cytoskeletal disruption associated with DLK overexpression.

result: Activating LZK in Purkinje cells causes slow, late-onset degeneration through JNK activation and apoptosis. PvalbCre/+;Hipp11-LZK(iOE)/+ mice survive to older adults (up to 8 months) but have low body weight. All lobular structures are present at P120. Morphological abnormalities appear around P15, with severity and cell loss increasing from P21 to P120. Cerebellum and molecular layer areas are significantly reduced. LZK expression is higher in anterior cerebellum, correlating with more severe Purkinje cell abnormalities and reduced MAP2 levels. Astrocyte reactivity increases from P21. LZK overexpression increases p-c-Jun and cleaved caspase-3 in Purkinje cells.
evaluation: Claims C7, C31, C81-C96 are well-supported by body weight data (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A-B), histological analysis (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C), Calbindin immunostaining showing progressive degeneration (Figure 4A-B), cerebellar area and molecular layer measurements (Figure 4C-D), tdTomato and LZK immunostaining showing regional differences (Figure 4E, Figure 4—figure supplement 1D-E), MAP2 staining (Figure 4E), GFAP staining (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A-C), p-c-Jun immunostaining (Figure 4F), and cleaved caspase-3 staining (Figure 4G-H). The temporal progression and regional specificity are well-documented.

result: CELF2 deletion does not modify DLK-induced Purkinje cell degeneration. PvalbCre/+;Celf2fl/fl mice are indistinguishable from controls. PvalbCre/+;Celf2fl/fl;Hipp11-DLK(iOE)/+ mice show similar Purkinje cell degeneration phenotypes to PvalbCre/+;Hipp11-DLK(iOE)/+ mice. CELF2 deletion does not alter DLK expression levels or p-c-Jun induction. All pups have smaller cerebella, show morbidity and low body weight, and die around P21.
evaluation: Claims C9, C32, C100-C107 are supported by Calbindin immunostaining (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-F), DLK western blot (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I), p-c-Jun immunostaining (Figure 5—figure supplement 1J-L), cerebellar area measurements (Figure 5—figure supplement 1G), and body weight data (Figure 5—figure supplement 1H). The data consistently show no rescue effect of CELF2 deletion on DLK-induced phenotypes.

result: CELF2 deletion strongly attenuates LZK-induced Purkinje cell degeneration. PvalbCre/+;Celf2fl/fl;Hipp11-LZK(iOE)/+ mice show significantly improved behavioral phenotypes from P30 to P120, although reduced body weight remains. CELF2 deletion dramatically reduces Purkinje cell degeneration with significant improvement in dendrite morphology at P120, inhibits astrogliosis and microgliosis, rescues MAP2 and NF-200 reduction, and suppresses pinceau disorganization. CELF2 deletion reduces the mRNA ratio of Map2k7-S to Map2k7-L by ~20%.
evaluation: Claims C108-C115 are strongly supported by behavioral scoring (Figure 5A-E, Video 2), body weight data (Figure 5F), Calbindin immunostaining (Figure 5G-J), GFAP and IBA1 staining (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A-D), MAP2 and NF-200 immunostaining (Figure 5—figure supplement 3A-B), parvalbumin staining showing pinceau (Figure 5—figure supplement 3B-C), and qRT-PCR analysis of Map2k7 isoforms (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B). The rescue effect is comprehensive and well-documented.

result: CELF2 deletion attenuates LZK-induced JNK signaling and apoptosis. LZK expression levels are not altered by CELF2 deletion. CELF2 deletion significantly attenuates p-c-Jun intensity in Purkinje cells, reduces total TUNEL+ cells, eliminates TUNEL co-localization with Purkinje cells, and nearly eliminates cleaved caspase-3 signals in Purkinje cells. Western blot shows increased pro-apoptotic Bcl-xL cleavage products in LZK overexpression mice.
evaluation: Claims C116-C123 are supported by LZK western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A-B), p-c-Jun immunostaining and quantification (Figure 6A-B), TUNEL assays (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D-F), cleaved caspase-3 immunostaining (Figure 6C-D), and Bcl-xL western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,C). The data demonstrate that CELF2 deletion reduces JNK signaling and apoptosis markers, supporting MKK7 as a functional mediator of LZK signaling.

result: DLK and LZK induce Purkinje cell degeneration independently of each other. In PvalbCre/+;Map3k13KO/KO;Hipp11-DLK(iOE)/+ mice, Purkinje cell degeneration and astrogliosis proceed similarly to PvalbCre/+;Hipp11-DLK(iOE)/+ mice. LZK deletion does not affect p-c-Jun levels induced by DLK. All pups die by P21 with similar morbidity. Conversely, PvalbCre/+;Map3k12fl/fl;Hipp11-LZK(iOE)/+ mice resemble PvalbCre/+;Hipp11-LZK(iOE)/+ mice in slow degeneration. DLK deletion does not alter Purkinje cell degeneration, astrogliosis, or p-c-Jun levels induced by LZK.
evaluation: Claims C8, C126-C134, C139 are supported by Calbindin and GFAP immunostaining (Figure 7A-E for DLK; Figure 7F,H,J for LZK), p-c-Jun immunostaining (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-B for DLK; Figure 7—figure supplement 1D-E for LZK), quantification of Purkinje cell numbers, molecular layer thickness, cerebellar area, and GFAP intensity (Figure 7B-E,G-J), and body weight data (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C). The data consistently demonstrate independence of DLK and LZK signaling in Purkinje cells.

result: DLK and LZK are conserved MAP3Ks with similar biochemical properties that activate JNK via MKK4 or MKK7. These kinases are orthologs of C. elegans DLK-1 and Drosophila DLK/Wallenda, act as upstream kinases for JNK and p38 MAP kinase, and are key players in neuronal stress response. Both show broad expression in the nervous system. They undergo auto-activation via leucine-zipper-mediated dimerization dependent on protein abundance, making elevated expression a proxy for activation.
evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C12-C16, C27-C28, C97 are supported by extensive citations to prior literature throughout the manuscript. These are well-established facts about DLK and LZK from previous studies, providing the necessary background and rationale for the current work.

result: Prior literature on DLK and LZK functions in various contexts. Constitutive DLK KO mice die perinatally with altered brain development, but adult DLK deletion shows no abnormalities. DLK has context-dependent roles in regeneration, degeneration, and neurodegeneration models. LZK mediates astrogliosis and can cooperate with DLK in some injury models. DLK regulates microtubule stability and is localized to neuronal processes. MKK7 activity is regulated by alternative splicing controlled by CELF2. DLK and LZK can bind each other and have synergistic interactions in some contexts.
evaluation: Claims C17-C26, C33-C34, C40, C48, C71-C72, C77, C98-C99, C124-C125, C141-C143, C145-C146, C148, C154-C155, C160, C162 are supported by citations to prior literature. These claims accurately represent established knowledge from previous studies and provide important context for interpreting the current findings.

result: Discussion and interpretation of findings. The authors conclude that controlling DLK and LZK activity levels is critical for neuronal survival and health. DLK triggers rapid degeneration while LZK causes slow degeneration, each activating JNK and inducing apoptosis independently. CELF2 deletion strongly attenuates LZK-induced but not DLK-induced degeneration. The differential effects may relate to signaling strength and kinetics. The findings are consistent with known roles of DLK in cytoskeleton regulation. The transgenic mice offer valuable models for studying cell-type and context-dependent kinase signaling.
evaluation: Claims C4, C11, C135-C138, C140, C144, C147, C149-C153, C156-C159, C161, C163-C167 represent interpretations and conclusions drawn from the experimental data. These are generally well-supported by the data presented, though some (C150, C152-C153, C163-C165) involve speculation about mechanisms. The interpretations are reasonable given the data, but some mechanistic details remain to be fully elucidated.
